findings.title: Success criterion 6's live non-SDK model dispatch has no task that closes it
findings.description: Success criterion 6 in the slice design requires two things: (a) a materialized `cf_workflow_status` executor returns actual project status — covered by Task 8.2 and walkthrough step 2 in Task 9.1 — and (b) "a dispatch with a tool-capable non-SDK model can call `cf_build_context` and receive assembled context (walkthrough §4)." Task 9.1 explicitly runs only walkthrough steps 1–3, and Task 9.3 records that step 4 "remains open alongside 263's demo." No task in the breakdown performs or schedules the criterion-6 dispatch. The environmental constraint (the `sq run` CLAUDECODE guard refuses inside Claude Code) is real and correctly documented, but as written the criterion is closed by no completable task — a reviewer checking criteria against tasks will find this one unmet. Recommend either adding a task that runs the step-4 pipeline from a standard terminal, or amending the slice design's success criterion 6 to explicitly scope step 4 as a deferred/manual verification with a named owner.

findings.title: Non-text-block result-mapping rule is implemented but never tested
findings.description: The design's Result mapping rules include "Non-text blocks are noted by type in the content, not dropped silently" (slice design line 137), and Task 4.4.2 implements it (task file line 137). Success criterion 2 says executors must map "results per the Result mapping rules." The Task 3 fake server provides fixtures for the other three rules (`echo` → text join, `fail` → isError, `empty` → zero blocks), but no fixture emits a non-text block (e.g., an image or resource block), and Task 5's test list has no case for it. If the non-text path regresses to silent-drop, the suite stays green. Suggest adding one fake-server tool returning a non-text block plus one assertion in Task 5.1; alternatively, confirm this rule is behavior-only and doesn't require a test.

findings.title: Commit guidance is expressed as checkbox success-criteria lines, not plain `**Commit**:` markers
findings.description: There are no `**Commit**:` markers in the file; commit instructions live in the "Commit protocol" section (line 57) and as `[ ]`-checkbox lines inside each task's success criteria (lines 84, 96, 120, 152, 182, 220, 251, 274, 299). Per the review rules a file with no markers is acceptable, and placement is substantively correct — one commit per task, after that task's scoped tests pass, neither after every subtask nor only at the end. Flagging only for format awareness: if the plain-line marker convention is desired, these would need to be lifted out of the checkboxes.

findings.title: Task 2 is small enough to fold into Task 1, but sequencing is correct as-is
findings.description: Task 2 adds two default-value assertions for the keys Task 1 just created — roughly a 5-line diff split into its own task with its own commit. It doesn't violate any rule (tests immediately follow implementation, effort is 1/5, no wasted setup), and the breakdown's stated sequencing rationale covers it. Noted only as a possible merge candidate if task count matters; not blocking.
